subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <bitset> header. SHIPPED 2026-08-25. 14 of 17 catalogued symbols across 3 headers. Back-ported to C++11; most const observers are constexpr from C++11 and the mutators from C++14, where std did not reach constexpr until C++23. THREE SYMBOLS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: the basic_string constructor, to_string, and the stream operators, all of which need headers that have not shipped. They are absent rather than approximated. The const char* constructor is provided and covers the common case. Verified against libstdc++ std::bitset at C++14/17/20.
legend_blurb: <bitset> is a fixed-size sequence of bits with the full bitwise operator surface. Its correctness rests on one invariant: the unused high bits of the last storage word are always zero.

symbols.name: bitset<N>
symbols.notes: Packed into ceil(N/64) unsigned long long words. THE TRIMMING INVARIANT is load-bearing: the unused high bits of the last word are always zero, and every mutator re-trims. count(), any() and operator== all read whole words, so a stray bit above N-1 would make a bitset compare unequal to itself after a flip. A zero-length bitset still allocates one word, because a zero-length array is ill-formed.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- see the OPEN tier-floor item.

symbols.name: bitset::reference
symbols.notes: operator[] on a non-const bitset returns a proxy, not a bool&, because a bit has no address. Holds the owner and index; operator= writes back.
